name: Giant's Causeway and Causeway Coast
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: On the north coast of County Antrim in Northern Ireland, the Giant's Causeway is a shoreline of about 40,000 interlocking black basalt columns, most of them hexagonal. Their flat tops form stepping stones that run from the cliff foot into the sea. The columns formed from volcanic eruptions 50–60 million years ago, and legend says a giant built them to stride across to Scotland. The tallest reach about 12 metres.
